newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy PM warns against govt crisis before May '98.
newsitem.headline: Italy PM warns against govt crisis before May '98.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that if his government fell before founder members of the European single currency were selected in May 1998, Italy would be ruined.
Addressing the Senate (upper house) at the end of a confidence debate in his centre-left administration, Prodi said Italy could not afford to be without a government for one day over the next year.

Prodi was forced to call a do-or-die confidence motion in both the upper and lower houses of parliament over the next three days after its hard left allies deserted government ranks on Wednesday in a vote over the deployment of a security force in Albania.
"A crisis in this period (before May 1998), would ruin this country because until May we cannot interrupt by as much as one day our efforts at overhauling (state accounts)," Prodi said.
The hard left Communist Refoundation, which secures Prodi's majority in the lower house of parliament, has pledged to support the government in the confidence vote.
Prodi said it was essential for Italy to carry on reducing interest rates, saying this was the best way to salvage the heavily-indebted economy.

He said the three percentage point fall in rates seen since his government took office last May, would lead to an annual saving of 60 trillion lire in reduced debt servicing costs. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
